S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.notes: Agent misreads structured data from tool responses: wrong flight selected, wrong item matched to specs, wrong cheapest/most-expensive identified, wrong product ID resolved

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.notes: Correct tool called but wrong arguments: wrong item ID, wrong payment method, wrong address details, wrong flight selection arguments

S3.label: Multi-step task completion
S3.notes: Drops sub-tasks, executes in wrong order, misses items in bulk operations, stops after partial completion without handling remaining items

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.notes: Acts without checking preconditions (basic economy no-refund policy, delay verification, payment policy), caves to user pressure and issues unwarranted compensation or violates policy

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.notes: Arithmetic errors in payment splits (certificate + gift card + credit card totals), flight price comparisons (earlier vs later time), refund calculations

S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.notes: Failures where agent needed to reason across multiple structured records simultaneously — e.g., comparing reservation details, finding duplicates, computing gift card/cert totals correctly.

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.notes: Agent called tools with wrong arguments: wrong reservation IDs, wrong flight numbers, wrong payment methods, wrong passenger counts, wrong item IDs.

S3.label: Multi-step completion
S3.notes: The dominant retail failure mode. Agent abandoned or failed to complete all requested sub-tasks (e.g., multiple exchanges across orders, cancel+modify, address+item changes). Many tasks require 3-5 tool sequences across different orders.

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.notes: The dominant airline failure mode. Agent violated policies by: cancelling non-refundable reservations, modifying basic economy flights, changing origin/destination, removing passengers, issuing unearned compensation, accepting invalid insurance claims.

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.notes: Failures involving incorrect calculations: wrong compensation amounts, wrong cheapest-flight selection, wrong payment splits (gift card + certificate + credit card), wrong total costs, wrong flight duration comparisons.

S6.label: Record discovery
S6.notes: Agent looked up the wrong reservation/order, failed to identify the correct flight/item from context (e.g., 'most recent order', 'the ATL flight', 'the order sent to Texas'), or failed to locate user by name/zip.

S7.label: Information communication
S7.notes: No clear cases where the agent knew the right answer but communicated it incorrectly.

S8.label: Conditional/state reasoning
S8.notes: Agent failed to apply user-stated conditional logic: 'if X then Y else Z' user instructions, mid-conversation intent changes (user changes mind at confirmation), ordering preferences (prefer AC adapter > battery > USB), and state transitions (order already in exchange-requested status so can't do another exchange).

S11.label: Tone/empathy
S11.notes: A9: Agent became entrapped in flattery/emotional manipulation loop, never completing the requested actions. A36: Agent overrode basic-economy policy due to user's tragic personal story (wife died).

S12.label: Hallucination of tools
S12.notes: R65: Agent claimed order was processed and couldn't be modified (false), then attempted workarounds. R76: Agent called modify tool with new_item_id same as old (tool error: 'new item id should be different from old item id'), indicating hallucinated/confused item resolution.

S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.description: Agent picks wrong item IDs, misidentifies reservation details, confuses passenger/payment structures, or applies actions to wrong records.

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.description: Wrong tool arguments (payment_id, item_ids, flight numbers, order IDs), wrong tool selected, or missing mandatory tool call. Most common failure across both domains.

S3.label: Multi-step completion
S3.description: Agent stops before completing all required steps, misses secondary tasks in multi-intent conversations, or fails to chain dependent operations correctly.

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.description: Agent ignores or misapplies policy constraints: cancels non-refundable reservations, modifies basic economy flights, issues wrong compensation amounts, or allows prohibited operations.

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.description: Wrong price comparison to find cheapest option, wrong certificate amount, incorrect total calculation, or wrong flight duration reasoning.

S6.label: Record discovery
S6.description: Agent fails to find the correct user account, reservation, or product record. Includes lookup failures, wrong order selection, and not discovering all relevant records.

S7.label: Information communication
S7.description: Agent completes the correct actions but fails to communicate required specific information (tracking numbers, price differences, material specs) to the user.

S8.label: Conditional/state reasoning
S8.description: Agent fails to reason about flight/order status conditions, incorrectly interprets what actions are allowed given the current state, or applies wrong conditional logic.

S11.label: Tone/empathy
S11.description: A9: Agent becomes sycophantic and stops enforcing policy when user repeatedly flatters it. R80: Agent gets drawn into emotional conversation and fails to complete exchange.

S12.label: Hallucination of tools
S12.description: Agent calls wrong tool (e.g., modify_user_address instead of modify_pending_order_address, uses item_id as product_id, wrong order ID format like #9502127 vs #W9502127), or transfers to human unnecessarily.

S1.name: Structured data reasoning

S2.name: Tool calling precision
S2.notes: Agent calls tools with wrong arguments or wrong tool entirely. In retail: exchanges with wrong item IDs, wrong payment methods, or proceeds without user confirmation. In airline: wrong flight number, wrong cabin, wrong payment method.

S3.notes: Agent fails to complete all requested actions in multi-action sessions. Common patterns: completes first request, forgets second; or abandons mid-task; or reaches max_steps before finishing. Most prevalent failure mode in retail.

S5.name: Numerical reasoning
S5.notes: Agent miscalculates totals, savings, price differences, or compensation amounts. Also includes failure to find cheapest/most-expensive items numerically. Often results in wrong refund figures or wrong flight chosen.

S6.name: Record discovery
S6.notes: Agent cannot locate the correct order, reservation, item, address, or flight from ambiguous user descriptions (e.g., 'most recent order', 'the NY address in my other order', 'second cheapest flight'). Requires scanning across multiple records.

S7.name: Information communication
S7.notes: Agent completes the action correctly but fails to explicitly communicate a required numeric value or piece of information (tracking number, balance, refund amount, total savings). Causes communicate_checks failures.

S8.name: Conditional/state reasoning
S8.notes: Agent cannot handle if-then branching: user changes mind mid-conversation, fallback chains ('if A not possible, do B'), or topic switches. Agent either ignores the conditional or treats it as unconditional.

S9.name: Language fluency
S9.notes: Agent produced an incoherent, poetic/jailbroken response when user praised it excessively. Evidence of susceptibility to sycophantic manipulation causing complete response degradation.

S11.name: Tone/empathy
S11.notes: Agent capitulates to emotional appeals (bereavement, anger about product quality, unhappy customer) and executes policy-violating actions. Separate from S4: the root trigger here is the emotional framing, not just a missing precondition check.

S12.name: Hallucination of tools
S12.notes: Agent repeatedly attempted tool calls that consistently errored (too_many_errors termination), suggesting it hallucinated or misapplied available tool signatures rather than recognizing that the operation is not supported.

S14.name: Context window mgmt
S14.notes: Tasks terminated at max_steps. Agent lost track of prior conversation state, repeated already-attempted actions, or failed to make progress across a long multi-step session.

S1.description: Structured data reasoning: reasoning over flight durations, product specifications across multiple records

S2.description: Tool calling precision: incorrect item IDs, wrong payment method routing, wrong tool parameters leading to DB mismatches

S3.description: Multi-step completion: failing to complete all required actions across multiple orders/reservations, or losing track mid-conversation

S4.description: Precondition verification: failing to check cancellation eligibility, basic economy restrictions, origin/destination change prohibition, insurance coverage requirements

S5.description: Numerical reasoning: incorrect payment splits, wrong certificate/gift card math, wrong compensation amounts

S6.description: Record discovery: failing to find correct reservations, wrong order IDs, inability to locate user accounts, missing relevant records

S7.description: Information communication: DB succeeded but failed to communicate required details (refund amounts, item specifications, tracking numbers)

S8.description: Conditional/state reasoning: wrong order state transitions, failure to adapt when initial action changes order status, misreading conditional task instructions

S9.description: Language fluency: no clear evidence of failures attributable to language generation quality

S10.description: Response latency: not measurable from conversation logs

S11.description: Tone/empathy: failing to hold policy under social pressure, or failing to explain difficult news empathetically

S12.description: Hallucination of tools: attempting invalid tool call sequences (remove item without replacement, exchange non-pending orders), or accepting user claims not in system data

S13.description: Format compliance: no clear evidence of format-specific failures

S14.description: Context window management: getting stuck in repetitive loops, failing to recognize conversation completion, losing track of task state over long conversations

S15.description: Multilingual handling: French-language request may have affected policy comprehension

S16.description: Proactive upselling: no evidence of failures in this dimension

focus: User deception cases - tasks where user provided false information, manipulated the agent, or the agent was deceived into violating policy
Multi-tool-call sequences - tasks where the agent made multiple sequential tool calls and the chain broke down, or called tools in wrong order or with wrong arguments
Recurring error patterns - grouping failures by systematic root causes that appear repeatedly across multiple tasks

S1.pattern: Agent failed to look up or communicate factual product/order information correctly

S2.pattern: Agent invoked the wrong tool, used wrong arguments (item IDs, reservation IDs, payment IDs), or called tools unnecessarily

S3.pattern: Agent failed to complete all required steps in multi-step tasks, especially when tasks required sequential or conditional actions

S4.pattern: Agent failed to verify preconditions before taking action (e.g., cancellation rules, modification eligibility, refund policy conditions)

S5.pattern: Agent made arithmetic errors in price calculations, payment splits, or refund amounts

S6.pattern: Agent failed to locate the correct record (reservation, order, flight) when given incomplete or indirect identifiers

S7.pattern: Agent communicated incorrect or incomplete information to the user (e.g., wrong material, missing tracking number)

S8.pattern: Agent failed to reason about conditional or stateful scenarios (e.g., if-then policy branches, order status affecting allowed actions)

S11.pattern: Agent was manipulated by user emotional framing to offer unauthorized compensation or bypass policy

S12.pattern: Agent hallucinated a tool call or used a non-existent tool name

S14.pattern: Agent ran out of conversation steps without completing the task due to excessive repetitive exchanges

S15.pattern: Agent did not handle French-language inputs correctly (A39: user switched to French mid-conversation)

focus: QA tester perspective - categorizing failures as distinct bug classes: policy enforcement bugs, calculation bugs, state machine bugs, search/lookup bugs, and compliance bugs

S1.bug_class: Information accuracy bug - agent reported wrong product attributes or order details

S2.bug_class: Tool invocation bug - agent called wrong tool, passed wrong IDs, or called tools with invalid argument combinations

S3.bug_class: Task completion bug - agent stopped short of completing all required steps, especially in multi-request conversations

S4.bug_class: Policy enforcement bug - agent bypassed or misapplied policy rules (cancellation criteria, cabin change restrictions, compensation thresholds)

S5.bug_class: Numerical reasoning bug - agent made errors in price totals, payment breakdowns, or comparing numeric flight durations

S6.bug_class: Record lookup bug - agent could not locate correct order/reservation/user when given incomplete or ambiguous identifiers

S7.bug_class: Communication accuracy bug - agent stated incorrect facts (wrong material, wrong price) in its response to the user

S8.bug_class: State machine bug - agent failed to handle conditional logic based on order/flight status (e.g., attempting exchange on returned order, modifying non-pending order)

S11.bug_class: Empathy manipulation bug - agent caved to social pressure and issued unauthorized compensation or violated policy to satisfy an emotionally distressed user

S12.bug_class: Hallucination bug - agent referenced or attempted to call a non-existent tool

S14.bug_class: Context management bug - agent got trapped in an unproductive loop, consuming all available steps without task completion

S15.bug_class: Multilingual handling bug - agent cancelled all reservations including non-refundable ones after user switched to French, failing to verify policy compliance

contrast_notes.key_contrast: Passed tasks typically involve: (1) single clear action, (2) policy conditions already satisfied, (3) no multi-step dependencies, (4) no user deception. Failed tasks cluster around: policy boundary cases, multi-step sequences with state dependencies, arithmetic over payment splits, and cases where user provided deceptive or ambiguous information.

S1.contrast: Passed tasks that required only info lookup (e.g., A3 baggage allowance, R13 tracking number) succeeded. Failed tasks like R3 and R21 required cross-referencing multiple product variants - a harder form of S1

S2.contrast: Passed tasks used simple 1-2 tool sequences. Failed tasks needed 5+ chained tool calls with payment IDs, flight IDs from intermediate results - much harder to get right

S3.contrast: Passed tasks typically required 1-2 atomic actions. Failed multi-step tasks like A37 (cancel 2, upgrade 1), A44 (cancel flights>4h, upgrade flights<=3h) required tracking multiple dependent state changes

S4.contrast: Passed tasks like A0 (cancel with clear criteria), A4 (correctly refused unauthorized compensation) show agent can handle simple policy checks. Failed tasks involved edge cases: agent bypassed policy when user applied social pressure (A2, A27, A38) or failed to check all preconditions before acting (A11, A26, A47)

S5.contrast: Passed tasks with payment involved single straightforward amounts. Failed tasks like A20 had complex certificate splitting logic, A25 had insurance calculations compounding errors

S6.contrast: Passed tasks provided explicit order/reservation IDs. Failed tasks required searching across multiple reservations by date range or flight route - harder discovery

S7.contrast: Passed info tasks like A3 answered correctly. R24 failed because agent said both t-shirts were cotton when one was polyester; R103 communicated wrong tracking number context

S8.contrast: Passed tasks had clear deterministic conditions. Failed tasks like A26 (cancel without meeting any criteria), R19 (exchange after return changes status), R27 (exchange blocked by prior return call) required reasoning about how earlier actions change allowed subsequent actions

S11.contrast: Passed task A5 correctly issued $50 cert to gold member per policy. A2 issued $300 (vs policy $100), A27 cancelled wrong reservation after user pressure, A38 issued cert for unverified delay claim

S12.contrast: All other tasks used real tool names. R76 uniquely showed agent hallucinating a non-existent tool call

S14.contrast: A9 hit max_steps because after task completion the user kept flattering the agent and the agent kept responding, wasting turns

S15.contrast: A39 user switched to French mid-conversation; agent cancelled all reservations including non-cancellable ones, failing to re-verify policy for each

Run 22: RL-trainability lens. Focus on skills where the model made a clear error that could be corrected via reward signal. Excludes cases where failure was purely environment/ambiguity. Airline prefix A, retail prefix R.

Run 23: Subtle pattern detection. Looking for non-obvious skill failures beyond the primary error — second-order issues like tone overriding policy, context tracking across turns, and preference ordering. Airline prefix A, retail prefix R.

Run 24: Strict/critical. Only assign a skill when there is direct, unambiguous evidence in the conversation. Skipped assignments where failure could be attributed to task ambiguity or tied to multiple plausible skills. Airline prefix A, retail prefix R.

Run 25: Impact-focused. Assign skills that, if improved, would most directly fix the failure. Prioritizes the single most impactful skill per task but allows a second when clearly co-causal. Airline prefix A, retail prefix R.
